items.title: Nine Years' War
items.why: The 1688 to 1697 war between France and the Grand Alliance.

items.title: War of the First Coalition
items.why: The 1792 to 1797 war against Revolutionary France. Its span sits inside the French Revolutionary Wars (1792 to 1802).

items.title: Treaty of Alcáçovas
items.why: The 1479 treaty that ended the War of the Castilian Succession and divided Atlantic claims between Castile and Portugal, the model for the Treaty of Tordesillas.

items.title: Treaty of Zaragoza
items.why: The 1529 treaty that settled the Moluccas dispute between Castile and Portugal and fixed the antimeridian to the Treaty of Tordesillas' line.

items.title: War of the Castilian Succession
items.why: The 1475 to 1479 war between Castile and Portugal that the Treaty of Alcáçovas ended.

items.title: Revolutions of Tunis
items.why: Re-queued: the lane row for Q3458428 was added to the seeds file on 14 October, so the item the writer refused for a missing lane now enters. The 1675 to 1705 uprisings against Ottoman Tunis. Africa trails every other lane.

items.title: Portuguese conquest of the East African coast
items.why: Africa trails every other lane. The 1500-1509 campaign that took Kilwa, Mombasa and Sofala for Portugal, part of the Indian Ocean monopoly the atlas already holds pieces of.

items.title: Battle of Mombasa (1505)
items.why: Africa trails. Francisco de Almeida's sack of Mombasa, a named action inside the East African coast campaign above.

items.title: Tripolitanian civil war
items.why: Africa trails. The 1793-1795 civil war in Ottoman Tripolitania, from the list of wars 1500-1799.

items.title: Dervish War
items.why: Africa trails. The Somali Dervish movement's war against Britain, Italy and Ethiopia, starting 1900, a P361 child of the Scramble for Africa the atlas already holds.

items.title: Italian Somali Wars
items.why: Africa trails. Italy's 1890-1927 pacification campaigns in Somalia, a P361 child of the Scramble for Africa.

items.title: Rabih War
items.why: Africa trails. Rabih az-Zubayr's 1899-1901 war against France in the Lake Chad basin, a P361 child of the Scramble for Africa.

items.title: Mandingo Wars
items.why: Africa trails. Samori Ture's 1882-1898 wars against French expansion in West Africa, a P361 child of the Scramble for Africa.

items.title: 1890 British Ultimatum
items.why: Africa trails. Britain's ultimatum over Portugal's claim to the Mozambique-Angola corridor, a turning point the atlas's own Scramble for Africa holds no record of yet.

items.title: Portuguese conquest of Hormuz
items.why: Asia trails after Africa. The 1507 campaign that made Hormuz a Portuguese vassal state, closing the Persian Gulf to rivals.

items.title: Portuguese conquest of Goa
items.why: Asia trails. Albuquerque's 1510 conquest that made Goa the capital of the Estado da India, central to the atlas's own period.

items.title: Siege of Aden (1513)
items.why: Asia trails. Albuquerque's failed assault on Aden, the gateway Portugal never took.

items.title: Capture of Muscat (1507)
items.why: Asia trails. The first Portuguese capture of Muscat, part of the same 1507 Gulf campaign as the Hormuz conquest.

items.title: Lam Sơn uprising
items.why: Asia trails. Le Loi's 1418-1427 uprising that ended Ming occupation of Vietnam and founded the Le dynasty.

items.title: Siamese revolution of 1688
items.why: Asia trails. The 1688 revolt that ended French influence at the Siamese court and closed Ayutthaya to Europeans for a century.

items.title: Hong Kyŏngnae's Rebellion
items.why: Asia trails. The 1811-1812 peasant rebellion against the Joseon court in Korea.

items.title: Burmese–Siamese War (1759–1760)
items.why: Asia trails, from the list of wars 1500-1799. Alaungpaya's invasion of Siam, the first of the Burmese-Siamese wars.

items.title: Ottoman–Persian War (1505–1517)
items.why: Asia trails. The opening war between the Ottomans and the Safavids, contemporary with Portugal's own Gulf campaigns.

items.title: Third Anglo-Mysore War
items.why: Asia trails, from the list of wars 1800-1899 (started 1790). The war that broke Mysore's power under Tipu Sultan.

items.title: Dzungar–Qing Wars
items.why: Asia trails, from the list of wars 1500-1799. The seventy-year conflict that ended the last steppe empire to challenge China.

items.title: Sino-Nepalese War
items.why: Asia trails, from the list of wars 1500-1799. The 1788-1789 Qing intervention in Nepal.

items.title: Haitian Revolution
items.why: Americas, from the list of revolutions and rebellions. The only slave revolt that founded a state, 1791-1804.

items.title: Northwest Indian War
items.why: Americas, from the list of wars 1500-1799. The 1785-1795 war over the Northwest Territory, ended by the Treaty of Greenville.

items.title: Whiskey Rebellion
items.why: Americas, from the list of revolutions and rebellions. The 1791-1794 tax revolt that tested the new federal government's authority.

items.title: Pontiac's War
items.why: Americas, from the list of wars 1500-1799. The 1763-1766 Native American uprising against British rule in the Great Lakes.

items.title: Revolt of the Comuneros (Paraguay)
items.why: Americas, from the list of revolutions and rebellions. The 1721-1735 revolt of Paraguayan settlers against the Jesuit missions and colonial governors.

items.title: Fredonian Rebellion
items.why: Americas, from the list of revolutions and rebellions. The 1826-1827 attempt by Anglo settlers to break part of Texas from Mexico.

items.title: Demerara rebellion of 1823
items.why: Americas, from the list of revolutions and rebellions. One of the largest slave uprisings in the British Caribbean, which hastened abolition.

items.title: Cabanagem
items.why: Americas, from the list of revolutions and rebellions. The 1835-1840 popular revolt in Grão-Pará against the Brazilian imperial government.

items.title: New York Conspiracy of 1741
items.why: Americas, from the list of revolutions and rebellions. The alleged slave and poor-white conspiracy that ended in the colony's largest mass execution.

items.title: Irish Rebellion of 1798
items.why: Europe, from the list of revolutions and rebellions. The United Irishmen's rising against British rule, the largest of its century in Ireland.

items.title: Cologne War
items.why: Europe, from the list of wars 1500-1799. The 1583-1588 war over the Archbishopric of Cologne, an early confessional war of the Holy Roman Empire.

items.title: Anglo-Spanish War (1585–1604)
items.why: Europe, from the list of wars 1500-1799. The war that included the Spanish Armada and set England and Spain against each other for two decades.

items.title: Franco-Dutch War
items.why: Europe, from the list of wars 1500-1799. Louis XIV's 1672-1678 war against the Dutch Republic, which drew in most of western Europe.

items.title: Revolt of the Comuneros
items.why: Europe, from the list of revolutions and rebellions. The 1520-1522 revolt of Castilian towns against the young Charles I.

items.title: Third Silesian War
items.why: Europe, from the list of wars 1500-1799. The Prussian-Austrian war of 1756-1763 fought alongside the wider Seven Years' War.

items.title: German Peasants' War
items.why: Europe, from the list of revolutions and rebellions. The largest popular uprising in Europe before 1789, 1524-1525.

items.title: War of the Bavarian Succession
items.why: Europe, from the list of wars 1500-1799. The 1778-1779 war between Prussia and Austria over the Bavarian succession.

items.title: War in the Vendée
items.why: Europe, from the list of wars 1500-1799. The 1793-1796 counter-revolutionary rising against the French Republic.

items.title: Morean War
items.why: Europe, from the list of wars 1500-1799. The 1684-1699 Ottoman-Venetian war that briefly won Venice the Peloponnese.

items.title: Jacobite rising of 1745
items.why: Europe, from the list of wars 1500-1799. Charles Edward Stuart's attempt to restore the Stuarts, ended at Culloden.
